Rhode Island allows a credit equal to a percentage of that federal care credit, limited to the amount of Rhode Island income tax (so any excess is not refunded - it is nonrefundable).

_strings.@@2bb2983cb9eb: Credit for Income Taxes Paid to Another State — Rhode Island residents who also paid income tax to another state on income that is also taxed by Rhode Island. Authorized under R.I. Gen. Laws section 44-30-18. If income tax was paid to more than one other state, Form RI-1040MU must be used.
_strings.@@39811a15e67d: Property Tax Relief Credit (Form RI-1040H, the RI property-tax circuit breaker) — Must answer YES to ALL eligibility questions on Form RI-1040H Part 1: (A) domiciled in Rhode Island for all of 2023; (B) lived in a household or rented a dwelling that was subject to property tax in 2023; (C) current on property taxes or rent due on the homestead for 2023 and all prior years; (D) you OR your spouse were 65 years of age or older AND/OR disabled as of December 31, 2023; and (E) 2023 total household income was $37,870 or less. Both homeowners (Part 3, attach 2023 property tax bill) and renters (Part 4, attach 2023 lease or 3 rent receipts; rent paid is multiplied by 20% as deemed property tax) may claim it.

_strings.@@9fa6b5efb06d: Treaty conformity — RI conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from RI income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the RI return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: The RI-1040 resident return starts from federal adjusted gross income (RI-1040 Line 1: "Enter your federal adjusted gross income from Federal Form 1040 or Federal Form 1040-SR, line 11"), and the General Instructions state "the Rhode Island income tax is based on your federal adjusted gross income." RI taxable income is built only via the RI Schedule M modifications. I reviewed every one of the "Modifications INCREASING Federal AGI" on Schedule M (Lines 2a-2k, instructions pages I-8 to I-10): the add-backs are out-of-state municipal bond interest (2a), RI fiduciary adjustment (2b), recapture of Family Education Account modifications (2c), bonus depreciation (2d), recapture of Section 529 modifications (2e), recapture of previously-claimed tax-credit income (2f), pass-through entity tax (2h), unemployment compensation not in federal AGI (2i), taxable PPP loan amount (2j), and a reserved line (2k). NONE of these add back income that is exempt from federal tax under a U.S. income tax treaty. Because treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and RI has no add-back of it, it flows through and is not re-taxed by Rhode Island. Therefore RI conforms (treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed).

RI does not impose its own separate eligibility test - if you receive the federal EITC, you receive the RI EITC. You must claim the federal EITC (federal Form 1040/1040-SR, line 27) to claim the RI credit.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: RI-1040, Line 8: "RI income tax from Rhode Island Tax Table or Tax Computation Worksheet" (Line 7 "RI TAXABLE INCOME. Subtract line 6 from line 5. If zero or less, enter 0"; Line 5 = Line 3 modified federal AGI minus Line 4 RI standard deduction; Line 6 = number of exemptions x $4,700) This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply 2023 Form RI-1040, Line 3 'Modified Federal AGI' (Line 1 federal AGI from Federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11, combined with Line 2 net modifications from RI Schedule M; the instructions say to enter 0 on Line 2 if you have no modifications, in which case Line 3 equals federal AGI). Do NOT subtract anything yourself: the op subtracts the shipped RI standard deduction (Line 4) and the shipped $4,700-per-person exemptions (Line 6) to reach RI TAXABLE INCOME (Line 7), then applies the rate schedule. Adjudication note (two-pass): base is federal_agi — RI-1040 starts from federal AGI (line 1) and taxable_base is Line 3 modified federal AGI (federal AGI +/- RI Schedule M modifications); the op subtracts the standard deduction and $4,700-per-exemption Line 6 amount. Single rate schedule for every filing status: the 2023 Rhode Island Tax Rate Schedule is captioned 'FOR ALL FILING STATUS TYPES' — the same three brackets (3.75% to $73,450; 4.75% to $166,950; 5.99% above) apply to Single, MFJ, MFS, HoH, and Qualifying widow(er); the schedule is duplicated per status here. Qualifying widow(er)/surviving spouse maps to married_filing_jointly: the RI standard deduction chart lists Qualifying widow(er) at the same $20,050 as MFJ, so the mapping is exact. Tax-table mandate below $100,000: the 2023 RI Tax Table header states 'Use if your Rhode Island taxable income is less than $100,000. If your taxable income is $100,000 or more, use the Tax Rate Schedules located on page T-1.' The table uses $50 bands computed at the band midpoint (e.g. taxable income $25,300-$25,350 yields tax $950 = $25,325 x 3.75% rounded), so bracket math may differ by a few dollars within table bands; the filed form must use the table below $100,000. Standard-deduction and exemption PHASEOUT is NOT modeled: if RI-1040 Line 3 (modified federal AGI) exceeds $233,750, BOTH the standard deduction and the $4,700 exemptions phase down in 20-percentage-point steps (factors 0.8000/0.6000/0.4000/0.2000) per $6,700 increment of the excess (rounded up to a whole increment), and both are $0 once the excess is more than $26,800 (i.e. Line 3 above $260,550). This op ships the full amounts — taxpayers with Line 3 over $233,750 must use the Standard Deduction Worksheet and Exemption Worksheet from the 2023 RI Tax Rate Schedule and Worksheets page instead. Rhode Island does not allow the use of federal itemized deductions (2023 RI-1040 instructions, Line 4) — every filer takes the RI standard deduction shipped here; there is no itemized alternative to model. If someone else can claim you as a dependent on their return, your RI exemption amount is zero (2023 RI-1040 instructions, Line 6 NOTE) — not modeled; such filers should be computed with zero exemptions. taxable_base must be RI-1040 Line 3 (Modified Federal AGI = federal AGI plus/minus net RI Schedule M modifications). Schedule M modifications (e.g. out-of-state municipal bond interest add-back, US-government-interest subtraction, taxable-Social-Security and pension/annuity modifications, military service pension modification) are NOT computed by this op; with no modifications Line 3 equals federal AGI (Federal Form 1040/1040-SR, line 11). Printed-constant rounding in the rate schedule: the 'Pay' constants are rounded to the cent and each diverges from the exact cumulative bracket sum by +$0.005 — printed $2,754.38 vs exact $2,754.375 (3.75% x $73,450), and printed $7,195.63 vs exact $7,195.625. The instructions' RI Tax Computation Worksheet (p. I-11) subtraction amounts ($0.00 / $734.50 / $2,804.68) reproduce the exact marginal math to the tenth of a cent; this pack's brackets use the exact marginal math. Rhode Island's personal and dependent exemptions ARE base reductions (subtracted from income on Line 6 before the rate applies), so they are shipped as exemptions. By contrast, RI's credits — the 15% RI earned income credit (Line 14d), 25% of the federal child and dependent care credit (RI Schedule I, carried to Line 9a), credit for taxes paid to other states (Line 9b), the RI-1040H property-tax relief circuit breaker (Line 14c) — are subtracted from TAX, not income, and are NOT applied by this op. No mid-year 2023 rate change: the 3.75%/4.75%/5.99% structure and the $73,450/$166,950 breakpoints are the final inflation-adjusted figures from the December 2023 rate schedule the 2023 filing season used ('WHAT'S NEW FOR TAX YEAR 2023' lists only inflationary adjustments to the brackets, deduction, exemption, and phaseout amounts).
